hero.visual_description: A Unitree G1 humanoid robot is filmed in a laboratory beside a padded incline. An overhead safety tether connects the robot to a mobile gantry, and an operator stands at the left holding the gantry controller. The robot steps onto the padded surface, bends its torso forward and lowers a handheld tool toward the surface. The robot begins to raise its torso near the end of the excerpt. The original frame is retained, including the operator and safety apparatus. This selected seven-second motion excerpt is shown at original speed without sound. It does not show the complete trial or its later outcome.

segments.label: 02 / Stepping and bending with a tool

hero.visual_description: A Unitree G1 humanoid robot is filmed in a laboratory beside a padded incline. An overhead safety tether connects the robot to a mobile gantry. An operator stands at the left and holds the gantry controller. The robot takes steps onto the padded surface, bends forward and lowers a handheld tool toward the surface, then straightens. In the final seconds, the tether becomes taut and the gantry lifts the robot during reset. The original frame is retained, including the operator and safety apparatus. This 12-second excerpt is shown at the original speed without sound. The recording illustrates the movement and supervised setup; it does not by itself establish successful tool operation or unsupported autonomous performance.

highlights.layout: Full source frame is fitted within the lower 640 pixels of a 1280 x 720 canvas. The upper 80 pixels contain white labels on a charcoal background, clear of native player controls; no source footage is covered by text. Portrait footage has side bars.
highlights.visual_description: This silent 33-second montage contains three separate laboratory recordings at the original speed. A persistent label identifies each clip; two hard cuts mark the changes. Clip 1 (0.00–4.23 seconds) uses a portrait camera view. The G1 robot takes steps from the laboratory floor onto a padded incline, while an overhead safety tether and an operator holding the controller remain visible. Clip 2 (4.23–16.23 seconds) uses a landscape view: the robot steps forward, bends its torso and lowers a handheld tool toward the padded surface, then straightens. The final moments retain the gantry-assisted reset. Clip 3 (16.23–33.03 seconds) shows another trial: the robot takes steps, bends deeply over the padded surface, shifts backward into a low crouched posture, then brings its torso upright and rises. The gantry lifts the robot during the final reset. The mobile gantry, safety tether and operator remain in frame throughout the tool trials. These images show physical movements and the supervised experimental setting, not direct evidence of successful nailing, hammering or unsupported autonomous performance.

webIntegrationReview.resolvedFinding: The first export placed labels below the footage, where native player controls could cover them. The highlights were re-exported with an independent 80-pixel label band above the complete frame. Clip times, original speed, description track and source hashes were unchanged.
webIntegrationReview.visualReview: Desktop screenshots confirm the G1 robot remains visible in the title backdrop; the full-frame toggle shows the operator, gantry and full source images. Highlights sampled at 2.4, 9, 24 and 32 seconds show the three labeled source recordings and final safety-hoist reset in order. The top label band is unobstructed with the native controls visible.
webIntegrationReview.limitations: This is a focused media integration review, not complete WCAG or ADA certification. Desktop title backgrounds intentionally crop the source edges; full-frame view and mobile layout preserve the full source frame. Full visual descriptions are provided as HTML as well as WebVTT.
